We find that the light curves continue to rise at all frequencies during this time period, following a power law of about $F_\nu\propto t^3$ (compared to $F_\nu\propto t^{5.7}$ at $972-1400$ days), and reaching a peak luminosity of $L\approx 10^{40}$ erg s$^{-1}$
The multi-frequency data indicate that the peak frequency does not significantly evolve over the 1030-day span of our observations, while the peak flux density increases by an order of magnitude.

The observed behavior is consistent with two possible scenarios: (i) a delayed spherical outflow launched about 620 days post-disruption with a velocity of $\approx 0.3c$ and an energy of $\sim10^{50}$ erg, and (ii) a highly off-axis ($\approx 80-90^\circ$) relativistic jet

We find that the light curves continue to rise at all frequencies during this time period, following a power law of about $F_\nu\propto t^3$ (compared to $F_\nu\propto t^{5.7}$ at $972-1400$ days), and reaching a peak luminosity of $L\approx 10^{40}$ erg s$^{-1}$
Indeed, it has now exceeded the radio luminosity of any previous TDE other than the relativistic event Sw J1644+57, which at a comparable timescale is only about a factor of 3 times more luminous.
Thus, the physical evolution of the radius for a spherical outflow supports an outflow that was launched with a substantial delay of about 1.7 years relative to the discovery of optical emission.
In the time span of 970 to 2160 days, the outflow kinetic energy increases by a factor of $\approx40$ from $E_K\approx 5.5\times 10^{48}$ to $2.1\times 10^{50}$ erg.
We therefore conclude that if AT2018hyz harbors an off-axis jet, then its viewing angle is $\approx 80-90^{\circ}$.

Since $\nu_c$ has a strong dependence on the magnetic field strength, measuring its location directly from the data can help to determine the value of $\epsilon_B$ and whether the outflow deviates from equipartition.
Therefore, a direct measurement of $\nu_{\rm m}$ gives an independent constraint on $\Gamma$ and breaks the degeneracy between $\Gamma$ and $\theta_{\rm obs}$ in the equipartition analysis.
